solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Gin and whisky, they're divine

definitions.meaning: gin and whisky are strong drinks, distilled liquors
ghosts and other supernatural beings, beings of an otherworldly sort

explanation.walkthrough: The two readings are alcoholic drinks and supernatural beings; 'divine' is a loose fit for disembodied beings, as the blogger noted.
explanation.definitionFit: Distilled liquor is called by this plural noun, and so are supernatural beings or souls.

clue.text: Cram maintaining run is strong

indicators.note: maintaining means the word for cram holds the other letter inside it

parts.note: to cram for an exam is to study hard
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A student insists that keeping up revision while jogging makes you robust.
explanation.definitionFit: Robust and solidly built, a sturdy thing is strong and hard to break.

clue.text: Demand in relation to 50% off

parts.note: sis is short for sister, a relation

indicators.note: 50% off means only half of the word to is kept, its first letter

explanation.surface: A shopper presses for a half-price discount.
explanation.definitionFit: To demand something is to require it firmly and refuse to back down.

clue.text: Engrossed in heartless article, then relaxed

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word for article is removed

parts.note: the is the definite article
to have rested is to have relaxed

explanation.surface: A reader is absorbed in a cold piece of writing, then unwinds.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone engrossed in a thing is absorbed by it, keen and attentive.

clue.text: Polish scratch

definitions.meaning: to rub something hard to clean it
to cancel or abandon a plan or an event

explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' tempts with a capital as the nationality; it is the verb, rub clean.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub is to clean by hard rubbing, and also, informally, to cancel something.

clue.text: Almost flog Ray? That's inconsiderate

indicators.note: almost means the word for flog loses its final letter

parts.note: to flog goods is to sell them
a ray is a flat sea creature, a fish

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether nearly whipping a man called Ray would be thoughtless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flog' is the British slang sense, to sell, not to whip; 'Almost' cuts SELL to SEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who thinks only of their own interests is being thoughtless of others.

clue.text: Dissecting insects — it could be one's job

definitions.text: Dissecting insects — it could be one's job

indicators.note: dissecting means the letters of insects and it are cut apart and put back in a new order

explanation.surface: Cutting up bugs might well be a lab worker's profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dissecting' rearranges INSECTS IT, and the whole clue describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An entomologist cutting up bugs in the lab is a researcher doing science.

clue.text: When they're closed you can't see in or out

definitions.text: When they're closed you can't see in or out

parts.words: When they're closed you can't see in or out
parts.note: the clue describes the folds of skin that shut over the eyes, like shutters on a window

explanation.definitionFit: Eyelids, often just called this, cover the eyes when they shut.

clue.text: Recognised lonely individual

definitions.meaning: identified, as a scientist singles out a virus

explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: each of the three words is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A virus can be identified this way in a lab; a remote village is cut off; a single case stands apart.

clue.text: Delay His Excellency — one in government

parts.note: HE is the abbreviation for His Excellency, an ambassador's title

indicators.note: in means one letter is placed inside the word for government

parts.note: the state is the government of a country
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An ambassador's arrival is postponed by an official.
explanation.definitionFit: To pause or hold back before acting is to delay, both verbs.

clue.text: Out of bed and prepared for trouble

parts.note: someone out of bed is up
prepared means set, as in ready, set, go

explanation.surface: Someone is up and ready for whatever bother the day brings.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouble someone is to disturb or distress them, the verb sense of the word.

clue.text: Doris ran off, grabbing last bit of soap — the sign of a shower

indicators.note: grabbing means the rearranged letters take a piece inside them
off suggests the letters of Doris ran have gone wrong and are rearranged
last bit of means only the final letter of soap is used

explanation.surface: Doris dashes out of the bathroom clutching the end of the soap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns DORIS RAN into RAINDROS, and 'grabbing' puts P, the last letter of soap, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Drops of rain falling from the sky show that a passing burst of rain is under way.

clue.text: Recoiling from French writing and illustrating

parts.note: in French, de means from or of
scribing is an old word for writing

explanation.surface: Someone shrinks back from reading and drawing in French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recoiling' normally signals a turnaround, but nothing is turned round here; as the blogger says it only joins the pieces, so treat it as padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing a scene is painting it in words, picturing or depicting it for the reader.

clue.text: 'Dessert' or 'desert' — it will come back with time

indicators.note: come back means the word for desert is read from end to start

parts.note: to rat on someone is to desert or betray them

explanation.surface: A clue writer muses on the old spelling muddle between pudding and wasteland.
explanation.walkthrough: The two quoted words tempt you to think of spelling; 'desert' is the verb, to rat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit pie or sweet pastry tart is served as the pudding course of a meal.

clue.text: Completely tough Roth novel about university

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the other piece
novel means new, so the letters of tough Roth are made anew

explanation.surface: A hard-hitting Philip Roth novel is set on a college campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges the two words and 'about' puts U inside the result. Philip Roth was an American novelist, which makes 'novel' look like a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Throughout means all the way through, from start to finish, entirely.

clue.text: Mean host isn't prepared for shock

indicators.note: prepared suggests the letters are made up into a new form

explanation.surface: A stingy host who has not got anything ready gives the guests a nasty surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Great surprise or amazement is the feeling of being stunned by something unexpected.

clue.text: Watching old boy getting plateful

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a serving is a helping of food, a plateful

explanation.surface: A former pupil looks on as he gets a heap of food.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'old boy' is a former pupil of a British school.
explanation.definitionFit: Observing something is watching it carefully, the same present participle.

clue.text: Hold hairdresser's equipment

definitions.meaning: a wrestling grip in which the legs clamp an opponent
cutting blades used to trim hair

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a wrestling hold with the legs crossed round an opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of cutting blades is used by barbers, and the word names a leg-lock grip in wrestling.

clue.text: Train the Queen to manoeuvre

parts.note: the engine pulls a train, standing for it here
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A royal train is shunted about.
explanation.definitionFit: To engineer an outcome is to manoeuvre or contrive it skilfully, both verbs.

clue.text: Turning to grab at gossip

indicators.note: to grab means the word for turning takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: a conversion is a turning, a change from one thing to another

explanation.surface: Someone turns to snatch a bit of tittle-tattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' looks like a participle in the surface but is a noun, a change of belief or form.
explanation.definitionFit: Chat and talk between people, the exchange of news, is what gossip amounts to.

clue.text: Good ride up in the air — learner driver is in this?

definitions.text: Good ride up in the air — learner driver is in this?

indicators.note: is in means that letter goes inside the other pieces
up in the air means the letters of ride are tossed about and rearranged

parts.note: L is the plate a learner driver displays in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone learning to pilot an unpowered aircraft enjoys a smooth flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up in the air' rearranges the word ride and 'is in' places L between G and that. British learner drivers display an L plate.
explanation.definitionFit: An unpowered aircraft that floats on air currents gives a quiet flight.

clue.text: Hoped bit of light could be captured by page editor

indicators.note: captured by means the word for a bit of light is held inside the others

parts.note: a ray is a beam, a bit of light

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor hopes to get a shaft of sunlight on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: To have prayed for something is to have hoped earnestly that it would happen.

clue.text: Dirty, therefore I left

parts.note: so means therefore

explanation.surface: Someone concludes that since it was filthy, they walked out.
explanation.definitionFit: To soil something is to make it dirty; both are verbs meaning to stain.

clue.text: Deciphering unfinished Alan Turing rule initially concerning the numbers 0, 1, 3, 6, 10…

indicators.note: deciphering, as Turing did with codes, means the letters are worked over into a new order
unfinished means the name Alan loses its final letter
initially means just the first letter of rule is taken

explanation.surface: Codebreaker Alan Turing is pictured at work on a puzzle about a number sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts ALAN to ALA, 'initially' gives R from rule, and 'Deciphering' shuffles ALA + TURING + R. Alan Turing was the British wartime codebreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Those numbers are the triangular numbers, counts of dots that can be stacked in a triangle shape.

clue.text: Quarrel with a head of government in Parisian street

indicators.note: in means that letter goes inside the word for street

parts.note: rue is French for street

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of government

explanation.surface: A row breaks out with a minister on a Paris boulevard.
explanation.definitionFit: To quarrel is to argue, dispute or row with someone, both verbs.

clue.text: Returning at times to get one form of transport

indicators.note: returning means the word at is read backwards

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, times
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Sometimes, coming home, you need a cab.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab hired for a ride is a common way of getting about town.

clue.text: What surgeon might be doing — lecturing about physical exercise

indicators.note: about means the word for lecturing goes round the other piece

parts.note: orating is making a speech, lecturing
PE is the abbreviation for physical education or exercise

explanation.surface: A surgeon gives a talk on keeping fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon at work in theatre is carrying out surgery on a patient.

clue.text: In a strange manner, as Moet might get me?

definitions.meaning: taking the first and third letters of Moet, the odd-numbered ones, gives the word me

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as 'odd-ly': the odd letters of MoEt spell ME. Moet is a brand of champagne, which tempts a drinking reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangely or peculiarly, an adverb describing a weird way of behaving.

clue.text: Ordering track to go round ends of border nearest Delhi

indicators.note: to go round means the word for track is placed around the other letters

parts.note: a track on an album is a song

indicators.note: ends of means the final letters of the last three words are taken

explanation.surface: A railway line is laid around the edge of the frontier closest to the Indian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends of' gives R, T, I from border, nearest, Delhi; 'track' suggests railways but means SONG.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting things in order, arranging or classifying them, is sorting them.

clue.text: Correspondent: 'er editor's sandwiches put down on paper

indicators.note: sandwiches means the letters are held between the clue's words, enclosed within them

explanation.surface: A journalist writes about her editor's lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside correspondENT 'ER EDitor's.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter details is to write them in a record or form.
